\chapter{On the Highway}
\label{ch:ml-on-the-highway}
\hlchaptermodality{468}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say a national highway, a toll, a tunnel, a flyover and to pull over.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 468: I can say a national highway, a toll, a tunnel, a flyover and to pull over.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ദേശീയപാത} (dēśīyapāta)}{ദേശീയപാത (dēśīyapāta)}]{\ml{ദേശീയപാത} (dēśīyapāta) — a national highway}

\label{lesson:ML-C468-desiyapata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to unload, then the Malayalam for to pack.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ദേശീയപാത}}
\textbf{\ml{ദേശീയപാത}} — \emph{dēśīyapāta} — \textquotedblleft{}a national highway\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഞങ്ങളുടെ} \ml{ഗ്രാമം} \ml{ദേശീയപാതയ്ക്ക്} \ml{അടുത്താണ്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ñaṅṅaḷuṭe grāmaṁ dēśīyapātaykkŭ aṭuttāṇŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our village is near the national highway.
\end{quote}

\ml{ദേശീയ} means national, as in \ml{ദേശീയ} \ml{ഗാനം}, the national anthem; \ml{പാത} is a road or track.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ദേശീയപാത}} (\emph{dēśīyapāta}) is a Malayalam compound built from \ml{ദേശീയ}, national, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{deśīya}, \textquotedblleft{}belonging to a country\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), and \ml{പാത}, a road, whose origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dēśīyapāta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dēśīyapāta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ñaṅṅaḷuṭe grāmaṁ dēśīyapātaykkŭ aṭuttāṇŭ.} — Our village is near the national highway.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to unload, then the Malayalam for to pack, then say \emph{dēśīyapāta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ദേശീയപാത} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A national highway\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ടോൾ} (ṭōḷ)}{ടോൾ (ṭōḷ)}]{\ml{ടോൾ} (ṭōḷ) — a toll}

\label{lesson:ML-C468-tol}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to pack, then the Malayalam for a national highway.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ടോൾ}}
\textbf{\ml{ടോൾ}} — \emph{ṭōḷ} — \textquotedblleft{}a toll\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പാലം} \ml{കടക്കാൻ} \ml{ലോറികൾ} \ml{ടോൾ} \ml{കൊടുക്കണം}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pālaṁ kaṭakkān lōṟikaḷ ṭōḷ koṭukkaṇaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Lorries must pay a toll to cross the bridge.
\end{quote}

The place where it is paid is a \ml{ടോൾ} \ml{പ്ലാസ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ടോൾ}} (\emph{ṭōḷ}) was borrowed from English \emph{toll}, a charge for using a road or a bridge.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭōḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭōḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pālaṁ kaṭakkān lōṟikaḷ ṭōḷ koṭukkaṇaṁ.} — Lorries must pay a toll to cross the bridge.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to pack, then the Malayalam for a national highway, then say \emph{ṭōḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ടോൾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A toll\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{തുരങ്കം} (turaṅkaṁ)}{തുരങ്കം (turaṅkaṁ)}]{\ml{തുരങ്കം} (turaṅkaṁ) — a tunnel}

\label{lesson:ML-C468-turankam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a national highway, then the Malayalam for a toll.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തുരങ്കം}}
\textbf{\ml{തുരങ്കം}} — \emph{turaṅkaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a tunnel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{തീവണ്ടി} \ml{മലയിലെ} \ml{നീളമുള്ള} \ml{തുരങ്കത്തിലൂടെ} \ml{പോയി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tīvaṇṭi malayile nīḷamuḷḷa turaṅkattilūṭe pōyi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The train went through a long tunnel in the hills.
\end{quote}

A -\ml{ം} noun: before an ending the -\ml{ം} becomes -\ml{ത്ത്}-, as in \ml{തുരങ്കത്തിൽ}, in the tunnel.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{തുരങ്കം}} (\emph{turaṅkaṁ}) is usually traced to Sanskrit \emph{suruṅgā}, \textquotedblleft{}a passage dug underground\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams); how the s- of the Sanskrit word became t- in Malayalam is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{turaṅkaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{turaṅkaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīvaṇṭi malayile nīḷamuḷḷa turaṅkattilūṭe pōyi.} — The train went through a long tunnel in the hills.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a national highway, then the Malayalam for a toll, then say \emph{turaṅkaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തുരങ്കം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A tunnel\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മേൽപ്പാലം} (mēlppālaṁ)}{മേൽപ്പാലം (mēlppālaṁ)}]{\ml{മേൽപ്പാലം} (mēlppālaṁ) — a flyover; an overbridge}

\label{lesson:ML-C468-melppalam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a toll, then the Malayalam for a tunnel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മേൽപ്പാലം}}
\textbf{\ml{മേൽപ്പാലം}} — \emph{mēlppālaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a flyover; an overbridge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{നഗരത്തിൽ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{പുതിയ} \ml{മേൽപ്പാലം} \ml{പണിയുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nagarattil oru putiya mēlppālaṁ paṇiyunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A new flyover is being built in the city.
\end{quote}

Built from \ml{മേൽ}, above, and \ml{പാലം}, a bridge: a bridge that goes over the road.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മേൽപ്പാലം}} (\emph{mēlppālaṁ}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{മേൽ}, above (DEDR 5086), and \ml{പാലം}, a bridge (DEDR 4099).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mēlppālaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mēlppālaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nagarattil oru putiya mēlppālaṁ paṇiyunnu.} — A new flyover is being built in the city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a toll, then the Malayalam for a tunnel, then say \emph{mēlppālaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മേൽപ്പാലം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A flyover; an overbridge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തുക} (otukkinirttuka)}{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തുക (otukkinirttuka)}]{\ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തുക} (otukkinirttuka) — to pull over}

\label{lesson:ML-C468-otukkinirttuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a tunnel, then the Malayalam for a flyover.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തുക}} — \emph{otukkinirttuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to pull over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അയാൾ} \ml{കാർ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{മരത്തിന്റെ} \ml{അടുത്ത്} \ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ayāḷ kār oru marattinṟe aṭuttŭ otukkinirtti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He pulled the car over beside a tree.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തി}, \emph{otukkinirtti}.

\ml{ഒതുക്കുക} is to move a thing to one side; \ml{നിർത്തുക} is to stop it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തുക}} (\emph{otukkinirttuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{ഒതുക്കുക}, to put to one side (DEDR 973), and \ml{നിർത്തുക}, to make stop (DEDR 3675).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{otukkinirttuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{otukkinirttuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ayāḷ kār oru marattinṟe aṭuttŭ otukkinirtti.} — He pulled the car over beside a tree.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a tunnel, then the Malayalam for a flyover, then say \emph{otukkinirttuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pull over\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words for getting around}

\label{lesson:ML-R468-review-461-468}



\begin{quote}
Say the Malayalam for a platform and a bus conductor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a platform, a bus conductor, a fare, a queue, to travel
  \item a reservation, a berth, a compartment, to make a booking, to buy a ticket
  \item a terminal, a runway, an airline, to lift off, a luggage trolley
  \item customs, passport control, a checkpost, an inspection, a foreigner
  \item departure, arrival, a delay, to wait standing, to run and board
  \item a suitcase, a load, a porter, a cloakroom, to drag along
  \item goods, a lorry, to put on board, to unload, to pack
  \item a national highway, a toll, a tunnel, a flyover, to pull over
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A platform? (\textbf{\ml{പ്ലാറ്റ്ഫോം}}, \emph{plāṟṟphōṁ}.) A bus conductor? (\textbf{\ml{കണ്ടക്ടർ}}, \emph{kaṇṭakṭar}.) A fare? (\textbf{\ml{യാത്രാക്കൂലി}}, \emph{yātrākkūli}.) A queue? (\textbf{\ml{ക്യൂ}}, \emph{kyū}.) To travel? (\textbf{\ml{സഞ്ചരിക്കുക}}, \emph{sañcarikkuka}.) A reservation? (\textbf{\ml{റിസർവേഷൻ}}, \emph{ṟisarvēṣan}.) A berth? (\textbf{\ml{ബെർത്ത്}}, \emph{berttŭ}.) A compartment? (\textbf{\ml{കമ്പാർട്ട്മെന്റ്}}, \emph{kampārṭṭmenṟŭ}.) To make a booking? (\textbf{\ml{ബുക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}}, \emph{bukkŭ ceyyuka}.) To buy a ticket? (\textbf{\ml{ടിക്കറ്റെടുക്കുക}}, \emph{ṭikkaṟṟeṭukkuka}.) A terminal? (\textbf{\ml{ടെർമിനൽ}}, \emph{ṭerminal}.) A runway? (\textbf{\ml{റൺവേ}}, \emph{ṟaṇvē}.) An airline? (\textbf{\ml{വിമാനക്കമ്പനി}}, \emph{vimānakkampani}.) To lift off? (\textbf{\ml{പറന്നുയരുക}}, \emph{paṟannuyaruka}.) A luggage trolley? (\textbf{\ml{ട്രോളി}}, \emph{ṭrōḷi}.) Customs? (\textbf{\ml{കസ്റ്റംസ്}}, \emph{kasṟṟaṁsŭ}.) Passport control? (\textbf{\ml{എമിഗ്രേഷൻ}}, \emph{emigrēṣan}.) A checkpost? (\textbf{\ml{ചെക്ക്പോസ്റ്റ്}}, \emph{cekkpōsṟṟŭ}.) An inspection? (\textbf{\ml{പരിശോധന}}, \emph{pariśōdhana}.) A foreigner? (\textbf{\ml{വിദേശി}}, \emph{vidēśi}.) Departure? (\textbf{\ml{പുറപ്പെടൽ}}, \emph{puṟappeṭal}.) Arrival? (\textbf{\ml{വരവ്}}, \emph{varavŭ}.) A delay? (\textbf{\ml{കാലതാമസം}}, \emph{kālatāmasaṁ}.) To wait standing? (\textbf{\ml{കാത്തുനിൽക്കുക}}, \emph{kāttunilkkuka}.) To run and board? (\textbf{\ml{ഓടിക്കയറുക}}, \emph{ōṭikkayaṟuka}.) A suitcase? (\textbf{\ml{സ്യൂട്ട്കേസ്}}, \emph{syūṭṭkēsŭ}.) A load? (\textbf{\ml{ചുമട്}}, \emph{cumaṭŭ}.) A porter? (\textbf{\ml{പോർട്ടർ}}, \emph{pōrṭṭar}.) A cloakroom? (\textbf{\ml{ക്ലോക്ക്റൂം}}, \emph{klōkkṟūṁ}.) To drag along? (\textbf{\ml{വലിച്ചുകൊണ്ടുപോകുക}}, \emph{valiccukoṇṭupōkuka}.) Goods? (\textbf{\ml{ചരക്ക്}}, \emph{carakkŭ}.) A lorry? (\textbf{\ml{ലോറി}}, \emph{lōṟi}.) To put on board? (\textbf{\ml{കയറ്റുക}}, \emph{kayaṟṟuka}.) To unload? (\textbf{\ml{ഇറക്കുക}}, \emph{iṟakkuka}.) To pack? (\textbf{\ml{പാക്ക്} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}}, \emph{pākkŭ ceyyuka}.) A national highway? (\textbf{\ml{ദേശീയപാത}}, \emph{dēśīyapāta}.) A toll? (\textbf{\ml{ടോൾ}}, \emph{ṭōḷ}.) A tunnel? (\textbf{\ml{തുരങ്കം}}, \emph{turaṅkaṁ}.) A flyover? (\textbf{\ml{മേൽപ്പാലം}}, \emph{mēlppālaṁ}.) To pull over? (\textbf{\ml{ഒതുക്കിനിർത്തുക}}, \emph{otukkinirttuka}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
